section.title: org.osgi.service.log.admin
section.para: Log Admin Package Version 1.0.

Bundles wishing to use this package must list the package in the Import-Package header of the bundle's manifest. This package has two types of users: the consumers that use the API in this package and the providers that implement the API in this package.

listitem.para: LoggerAdmin - LoggerAdmin service for configuring loggers.
LoggerContext - Logger Context for a bundle.

section.title: public interface LoggerAdmin
section.para: LoggerAdmin service for configuring loggers.

Each bundle may have its own named LoggerContext based upon its bundle symbolic name, bundle version, and bundle location. There is also a root Logger Context from which each named Logger Context inherits. The root Logger Context has no name.

When a bundle logs, the logger implementation must locate the Logger Context for the bundle to determine the effective log level of the logger name. The best matching name for the Logger Context is the longest name, which has a non-empty Logger Context, according to this syntax:

The search stops at the first non-empty Logger Context. If no non-empty Logger Context is found using the above search order, the Logger Context with the symbolic name of the bundle must be used for the bundle.

formalpara.title: Provider Type
formalpara.para: Consumers of this API must not implement this type

section.title: public static final String LOG_SERVICE_ID = "osgi.log.service.id"
section.para: Logger Admin service property to associate the Logger Admin service with a LoggerFactory service.
This service property is set to the service.id for the LoggerFactory service administered by this Logger Admin.
The value of this service property must be of type Long.

section.title: public LoggerContext getLoggerContext(String name)

formalpara.title: name
formalpara.para: The name of the Logger Context. Can be null to specify the root Logger Context.

section.para: Get the Logger Context for the specified name.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The Logger Context for the specified name. The returned Logger Context may be empty.

section.title: public interface LoggerContext
section.para: Logger Context for a bundle.
Any change to the configuration of this Logger Context must be effective immediately for all loggers that would rely upon the configuration of this Logger Context.

formalpara.title: Provider Type
formalpara.para: Consumers of this API must not implement this type

section.title: public static final String LOGGER_CONTEXT_DEFAULT_LOGLEVEL = "org.osgi.service.log.admin.loglevel"
section.para: Framework launching property specifying the default log level of the root Logger Context.
The value of this property must be the name of the one of the LogLevels.
If not specified, or the specified value is not the name of the one of the LogLevels, the default log level of the root Logger Context is LogLevel.WARN.

section.title: public static final String LOGGER_CONTEXT_PID = "org.osgi.service.log.admin"
section.para: Logger Context PID.

If Configuration Admin is present, Logger Context configuration information in Configuration Admin must be used. The name of the Logger Context is mapped to a Configuration Admin targeted PID as follows:

listitem.para: The root Logger Context, which has no name, is mapped to the PID org.osgi.service.log.admin.

A named Logger Context is mapped to a targeted PID by prefixing the Logger Context's name with org.osgi.service.log.admin followed by vertical line ('|' \u007c). For example, the Logger Context named com.foo.bar is mapped to the targeted PID org.osgi.service.log.admin|com.foo.bar.

section.title: public void clear()
section.para: Clear the configuration of this Logger Context.
The configured log levels will be cleared.

section.title: public LogLevel getEffectiveLogLevel(String name)
section.para: Returns the effective log level of the logger name in this Logger Context.
The effective log level for a logger name is found by the following steps:

listitem.para: If the specified logger name is configured with a log level, return the configured log level.
For each ancestor logger name of the specified logger name, if the ancestor logger name is configured with a log level, return the configured log level.
If this Logger Context is named, return the result of calling this method on the root Logger Context with the specified logger name.
If this Logger Context is the root Logger Context, return the default log level of the root Logger Context.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The effective log level of the logger name in this Logger Context.

section.title: public Map<String, LogLevel> getLogLevels()
section.para: Returns the configured log levels for this Logger Context.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The configured log levels for this Logger Context. The keys are the logger names and the values are the log levels. The returned map may be empty if no logger names are configured for this Logger Context. The returned map is the property of the caller who can modify the map and use it as input to setLogLevels(Map). The returned map must support all optional Map operations.

section.title: public String getName()
section.para: Returns the name for this Logger Context.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The name for this Logger Context. The root Logger Context has no name and returns null.

section.title: public boolean isEmpty()
section.para: Returns whether the configuration of this Logger Context is empty.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: true if this Logger Context has no configuration. That is, the configured log levels are empty. Otherwise false is returned.

section.title: public void setLogLevels(Map<String, LogLevel> logLevels)

formalpara.title: logLevels
formalpara.para: The log levels to configure for this Logger Context. The keys are the logger names and the values are the log levels. The specified map is the property of the caller and this method must not modify or retain the specified map.

section.para: Configure the log levels for this Logger Context.
All previous log levels configured for this Logger Context are cleared and then the log levels in the specified map are configured.

The configured log levels for this Logger Context can be set by both this method and by configuration information in Configuration Admin, if Configuration Admin is present. The configured log levels for this Logger Context are based upon the last technique used to update the configured log levels. This method must not modify or set configuration information in Configuration Admin.
